chunks: Charities are meant for the indigent and needy, and those who collect and distribute them, and those whom you wish to win over, and for redeeming slaves (and captives) and those who are burdened with debt, and in the cause of God, and the wayfarers: So does God ordain. God is all-knowing and all-wise.

key_terms.وَالْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا: And those who collect and distribute them
key_terms.وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ: And those whose hearts are to be won over (new converts)
key_terms.وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: And in the cause of God

ai.seo_question: Who are the eight categories of Zakat recipients mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this foundational verse (Ayat al-Zakat) is interpreted to include the 'Alamin' (distributors) as a distinct category, often linked to the Imam or his deputies, thereby supporting the collection of Khums. The mention of 'Fi al-Riqab' (in freeing slaves) is also understood by Shia scholars to include freeing captives and, by extension, paying off debts for those unable to do so, emphasizing social welfare. This divine ordinance underscores the spiritual and economic dimensions of purification, linking material distribution to God's wisdom and knowledge.
